name: recommendation
markdown: This patient with a 10-year history of type 2 diabetes and newly documented microalbuminuria (ACR 12 mg/mmol) requires urgent baseline renal biochemistry to stage possible diabetic nephropathy and guide further management [RULE: R-CKD-001]. Before any therapy adjustment or specialist review, serum creatinine and eGFR must be obtained within 7 days to quantify kidney function. Blood pressure control (currently 138/84 mmHg on ramipril 5 mg) and glycaemic control (HbA1c 58 mmol/mol) should be optimised in parallel, but dosing decisions depend on confirmed eGFR. Safety-net the patient to return if symptoms of fluid overload, worsening hypertension, or reduced urine output develop.

actions.rationale: Baseline renal function is essential to stage CKD and guide therapy in a diabetic patient with microalbuminuria.

actions.action: Review blood pressure and consider ACE-inhibitor titration once eGFR known
actions.rationale: Target BP <130/80 mmHg in diabetic CKD; current ramipril dose may require adjustment based on renal function.

actions.action: Safety-net patient to seek urgent review if symptoms of fluid overload or oliguria develop
actions.rationale: Early recognition of acute-on-chronic kidney injury is critical in this at-risk group.
